processing: Details are scarce. It is a green tea, heated to stop oxidation and shaped flat and straight, with a leaf wrapped around each bud.
harvest_season: Spring, when the young shoots are white.
appearance_dry: Flat, straight pieces with one leaf folded around one bud, compared to an orchid.
appearance_liquor: Typically pale and clear, as with other tender Zhejiang greens.
appearance_wet: Tender, pale pieces of bud and leaf, as the young spring shoots are noticeably white.
taste_profile: No detailed tasting record exists; as with other tender Zhejiang greens, expect a light, fresh and gently sweet cup.

brewing.notes: General advice for a tender green: use a glass, with water well off the boil.

vintage_note: Specific sales practice is not recorded. As is usual for Zhejiang greens, expect the current spring harvest, best drunk within the year.
description:
Anji Baipian, also called Yurui tea, is a flat green tea from Anji in Zhejiang. Its shape sets it apart: one leaf wrapped around one bud, straight and flat, likened to an orchid.

Its young spring shoots are unusually white, which may be where the name comes from. Beyond the shape, the details of how it is made are thinly recorded, so the rest is what applies to green tea generally.

There is little reliable tasting information. Brew it like other tender Zhejiang greens, with cooler water and short steeps, and let your own cup be the guide.

Anji Baipian and the better-known Anji Bai Cha come from the same county and are named side by side, so do not assume a seller means one when offering the other. Ask for the harvest date and how the leaf is shaped.
history: Little is documented about this tea's origin or who first made it. It is recorded as one of Zhejiang's named teas from Anji, named next to Anji Bai Cha, and how the two have related over time is not clear.
